narrative_purpose: Land Munk's stagger theorem visually: separating two wings along the flight direction does almost nothing, while separating them vertically lifts the rear wing out of the sinking air and fixes the problem.
subject: A split-frame comparison of two wing arrangements, divided by a clear vertical seam down the centre. LEFT HALF: two thin dark wing cross-sections at almost the same height as each other but placed very far apart horizontally; a broad band of pale cool-teal flowing lines sinks gently from the first one and the second one sits fully inside that band. RIGHT HALF: the same two wing sections placed close together horizontally but with a large vertical separation, the upper section clearly above the sinking band of flow, the flow lines reaching it staying horizontal and clean.
scene: An abstract dark field on both halves, nothing but the wing sections and the flowing air.
camera: Flat side elevation on both halves, identical scale and eye level so the comparison reads instantly.
light: Self-luminous pale flow lines against darkness; cool teal where the flow sinks and spoils the rear wing on the left, a cleaner brighter cyan for the undisturbed flow on the right.
palette: Left half muted teal-into-magenta where the rear wing sits in bad air; right half cleaner cyan. Deep indigo void behind both.
style: Painterly hand-worked comparison plate, brushed glowing flow, not a vector schematic.
detail_level: Even detail on both halves so neither reads as the more finished picture.
composition: Clean vertical split down the centre, matched framing, plain dark space along the top of each half framed by deep negative space.
consistency_notes: Wing sections identical in shape and size to the previous figure's, so the reader recognises them. Left = far apart along the flight direction and still spoiled; right = far apart vertically and clean. The contrast between 'inside the sinking air' and 'above it' is the only idea in the frame.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrowheads, no dimension lines, no vector-flat infographic look, no CAD linework, no photographic or 3D render, no cartoon style
